title: Uniform inverse-prime-square bound for first-order arithmetic singularity conditions in ample sections modulo p squared on smooth irreducible fibers of regular projective arithmetic varieties
source_title: On the Bertini regularity theorem for arithmetic varieties
author: Xiaozong Wang
difficulty_reason: A fixed-prime Bertini limit does not provide a bound uniform when the prime is larger than the section degree. Section6 proves a dimension-induction estimate for positive-dimensional singular loci and then separates high-degree points using a second p-adic lifting coordinate and uniform local evaluation bounds. The finite-field derivative-decoupling estimates and arithmetic tangent-space exact sequence remain substantive obligations before the final inverse-prime-square sum closes.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Proposition6.1: regular integral flat projective arithmetic variety of absolute dimension n over SpecZ, ample algebraic line bundle, all sufficiently large d uniformly, and ONLY primes p whose fiber X_p is smooth and irreducible. The uniform proportion bound c p^(-2) concerns sections modulo p² having a closed point with tangent-space dimension n rather than n−1; it is not a claim that the modulo-p² divisor itself is a regular scheme. Full new uniform finite-singular-locus Bezout bound, hyperplane dimension induction, low/high-degree splitting, p-adic lift separation49–51 and all required authored finite-field Appendix derivative-decoupling/local-coordinate support53–70 read. Existing Serre/ample multiplication, Lang–Weil, refined Bezout, Poonen finite-scheme polynomial evaluation are explicit foundations. Smooth irreducibility of each admitted fiber is essential, without inferring it for all large primes from mere generic integrality. In50 the evaluation exponent d/N is stronger than the provided minimum(degree(x),floor(d/N)); earlier48 states the applicable d/(Nn) bound explicitly. This weaker linear-in-d bound is sufficient for the exact author c p^(-2) conclusion and is a bounded ancillary minimum/degree bookkeeping check, not new high-degree Bertini construction. Hyperplane Bezout reduction uses generic linear combinations of the supplied derivatives after a finite field extension, as permitted by the stated refined Bezout/polynomial-evaluation constructions; no all-divisor regularity/global zeta-density theorem, Arakelov tail corollary or finite-field parameter variant counted separately.
